batch: Separate owned sprite geometry from SDL submission
classification: Structural refactor; no speedup claim and no production worker enabled

boundary.preparation: prepare_sprite_geometry takes owned values and returns destination, rotation/flip, and optional opaque footprint; no renderer, texture, map, Lua, scratch references, or RNG calls
boundary.renderer_owner: cata_tiles still selects sprite/texture/lighting, owns shaders and tint scratch, submits SDL copies, applies the legacy Direct3D adjustment, and updates ordered per-tile height
preserved_behavior: Negative pixel offsets floor; retraction interpolation truncates and clamps at endpoints
Isometric suppression, explicit horizontal mirror, manual rotations, and bullet diagonal codes retain existing behavior
Existing modulo-4 tint footprint retained separately from actual diagonal transform
Tint mask records pre-backend destination; gray silhouette uses submission destination
Foreground/background height accumulation unchanged; no save/Lua/network schema changes
boundary.parallel_contract_test: Four std::async jobs each own 64 mixed sprite inputs and return results in input order; producer inputs destroyed before joins; matches serial reference
boundary.production_threading: No new gameplay or renderer worker; resource submission remains on owning thread

Cross-process exact sprite pixels are not a deterministic gate. Geometry fixtures and actual screenshots inspected; differences not all attributed to animation.

existing_threading_followup.source_fact: sounds.cpp generate_melee_sound starts detached sound_thread; operator calls rng and reads calendar/player. rng.cpp returns shared global engine unless that thread called rng_set_worker_seed; melee thread does not register. This violates owned-state/RNG boundaries.
existing_threading_followup.causality: Likely contributor to observed old combat non-reproducibility; first differing RNG draw not traced. Audio and simulation code not changed in this batch.
existing_threading_followup.next_design: Close melee presentation job ownership first: capture immutable context on main owner, isolate presentation randomness, remove live world reads, and use a bounded scheduling/submission boundary. Preserve gameplay RNG/replay contracts with focused regressions before adding wider workers.
